newsitem.title: UK: Bodycote says trading in Q1 1997 strong.
newsitem.headline: Bodycote says trading in Q1 1997 strong.

text.p: Bodycote International Plc, the British engineering services company, said on Wednesday trading in the first quarter of 1997 has been strong and it is looking forward to another successful year.
The group reported a 48 percent jump in profits before tax and exceptionals to 27.2 million stg in the year to end-December 1996.

It said headline earnings per share, based on the weighted number of shares in issue during the year, were 29.5 pence, up 45 percent. It announced a total dividend of 7.4 pence per share, up 21 percent from the previous year's 6.1 pence.
"The results for the year reflect the continued progress and expansion of the group's technology activities in the UK, U.S. and Europe," Bodycote said in a statement accompanying the results.

It said 1996, when the company was admitted to the FTSE 250 share index, had been an eventual year. It made nine acquisitions, had a rights issue which raised 117 million stg, and then this year acquired the Swedish heat treatment group Brukens Thermotreat AB for 56 million stg.

"There are still immense opportunities, both geographically and technically, for further substantial development of the group," it said. "Accordingly, we expect 1997 to be a year of continued expansion, both organically and by acquisition".

Bodycote Metal Technology profits jumped by 53 percent to 27.1 million stg. During the year the group expanded from 56 to 101 operational centres as a result of organic expansion and acquisitions. The company said the full benefits of its acquisitions will be seen this year and beyond.
The 1996 figures for earnings and interim dividend, as well as the comparative figures for 1995, have been adjusted to take account of the one for three rights issue in December 1996.
